request: I sell provisions at Makola market and I want to keep track of my stock. For each item I want to save its name, how many I have, and the level at which I consider it to be running low. When I sell some of an item the quantity should go down, but I must not be able to sell more than I have. When new goods arrive I record a restock and the quantity goes up. The amount sold or restocked must always be more than zero. I want to see all my items, look at one item, and see a list of the items that are at or below their low level so I know what to buy.
summary:
I've built your stock tracker as a small web service (`app.py`). It saves everything in a file called `stock.db` in the same folder, so your stock is kept between restarts. I wrote 15 automated tests covering everything you asked for, and they all pass.

**What you can do with it:**

| Action | Address | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| Add an item | `POST /items` with `{"name": "Rice", "quantity": 20, "low_level": 5}` | Saves a new item. The name can't be blank, and the quantity and low level can't be negative. |
| See all items | `GET /items` | Lists every item. |
| Look at one item | `GET /items/{id}` | Shows one item, or a "not found" message if that number doesn't exist. |
| Record a sale | `POST /items/{id}/sell` with `{"amount": 3}` | Takes the amount off the quantity. If you try to sell more than you have, it refuses and your stock stays the same. Selling everything you have, down to 0, is allowed. |
| Record a restock | `POST /items/{id}/restock` with `{"amount": 10}` | Adds the amount to the quantity. |
| See what to buy | `GET /items/low` | Lists the items at or below their low level. |

**Things to know:**
- **Item numbers:** each item gets a number (its "id") when you add it, and you use that number to look at it, sell it or restock it.
- **Amounts must be above zero:** a sale or restock of 0 or less is refused and nothing changes.
- **Duplicate names are allowed:** adding "Rice" twice gives you two separate items, so it's best to add each item only once.
- **Test items in your list:** I ran the tests against the same `stock.db` file the app uses, so it now contains some practice items with names like "item-3f9a1c2b". Delete `stock.db` before you start entering your real stock, and the app will create a fresh, empty one the next time it starts.
